hazard: Inconsistent interpretation of antenatal CTG leading to delayed or inappropriate response
theme: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

reports.title: Isa Mushtaq
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: In clinical practice the fetal CTG continues to be a source of problems, both in interpretation and in what degree of action should be taken
concerns.hazard: inconsistent interpretation of antenatal CTG leading to delayed or inappropriate response

concerns.quote: Reliance on the NICE guidance for intrapartum CTG monitoring to interpret antenatal CTG features is of limited value because: (i) It is not intended for such use and therefore such practice is arguably not evidence based (ii) It is much more common for fetal heart traces not to look normal during labour (in the region 20 -30 % outwith normal parameters) therefore the significance of such abnormal traces may not be the same in labour as compared to when identified antenatally. (iii) Only a very
concerns.hazard: misapplication of intrapartum CTG guidance to antenatal monitoring

concerns.quote: There should be a review to consider whether national guidance on antepartum CTG monitoring and interpretation where there are abnormalities or unusual features would lead to safer, evidence based management of such cases
concerns.hazard: lack of national guidance for antepartum CTG abnormalities

reports.title: Maxim Karpovich
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: It was apparent that the Midwives involved with Maxim's birth and a Junior Obstetrician, appeared not to understand that the cardiotocograph (CTG) trace was abnormal on several occasions. The Obstetric Registrar, at 2357 hours, incorrectly classified the CTG to be normal when it clearly was not. The baby, Maxim, who was delivered by an emergency caesarean section. Expert evidence stated that if the caesarean section had been carried out by midnight, the baby would have survived, although there could
concerns.hazard: misinterpretation of CTG traces leading to missed abnormal fetal heart rate patterns

concerns.quote: Midwives and Obstetricians lack the core skills to interpret CTG tracings for intrapartum care
concerns.hazard: lack of core skills to interpret CTG tracings

concerns.quote: There is a need for the development of quality controlled training modules. Such courses should last for at least two days and cover the correct use of the CTG technology; foetal pathophysiology; understanding of the role of infection fever and meconium aspiration, trauma and other stresses and their interaction with asphyxia
concerns.hazard: absence of quality controlled CTG training modules

concerns.quote: There should be mandatory confirmation of competence at CTG interpretation with pass or fail testing before entering practice to determine the critical issues around the contents of intrapartum CTG training modules and the validity of associated tests
concerns.hazard: absence of mandatory competence testing for CTG interpretation

concerns.quote: This training should address pattern recognition, pathophysiology of foetal heart rate changes, clinical scenarios with CTG's and appropriate responses
concerns.hazard: lack of training on pattern recognition and clinical response to CTG changes

links.explanation: Both reports highlight deficiencies in interpreting cardiotocograph (CTG) traces that can lead to delayed clinical action. The earlier report focuses on lack of guidance for antenatal CTG, while the later report calls for training to improve intrapartum CTG interpretation.
